caseno: Writ Petition Nos. 5513- 5517 of 1996 and 6753, 6754 of 1997.
lawyer:
Khandaker Mahbubuddin Ahmed with Mahbubey Alam, advocates - For the Petitioners in all the Writ Petitions except Writ Petitions Nos. 6753 and 6754 of 1997.
Md Nawab Ali with Moisul Hoque, Advocates—For the Petitioners in Writ Petition Nos. 6753 and 6754 of 1997. 
AF Hasan Ariff with Md Badruddoza, Advocates — For the Respondent No. 4 in all the Writ Petitions. 
Fariduddin Khan, Assistant Attorney-General—For Respondent No. 3 in all the Writ Petitions.
parties:
Ameenah Ahmed and others ----- Petitioners
Vs. 
Bangladesh and ors ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
3. It is stated that the petitioners in possession owned about 8.50 acres of land of CS Plot Nos. 76, 77, 78, 79, 80, 81 and 82 of Mouza Baipale and CA Plot Nos. 731, 732, 733, 746 and 749 of Mouza Gonokbari are situated contiguously in a block and demarcated by iron grills and RCC Pillar with a height of 7 feet from the ground level. The petitioners acquired these lands by inheritance as well as through purchase and have been developing and maintaining it over a period of 30 years. It has been stated that there is a Katcha Mosque and several structures for the purpose of saying prayers and meditation for spiritual advancement and that the petitioners spent a huge amount of money for the development of the said land. The local people as well as the visitors from Bangladesh and abroad allegedly visited the said land and said prayers in the Katcha Mosque situated there as well as spent time in meditation in the said area for spiritual salvation and advancement. It is further stated that the petitioners started Agro-based Industry to meet the cost of maintenance for running the aforesaid centre for worship and meditation and that at least 20 to 25 regular workers are working there with their families and depend on the income of Agro Industry. It is further stated that there are several valuable trees planted by important dignitaries and persons in the said area. It is further stated that there is a highway in front of the aforesaid plots of the petitioners and on its other side the Export Processing Zone is situated and that if the authority takes the contiguous land adjacent to the existing BEPZA boundary line it would affect the land owned by a former influential Cabinet Minister. It is alleged that the respondents with malaise intention and being illegally influenced by the interested persons, have decided to acquire the land of the petitioners which is on the other side of the road. It is further stated that the petitioners and their family members are situated in the extreme west southern corner of the proposed acquisition and though the respondents have huge land besides the land of the petitioners and their family members the land of the petitioners has been chosen at the instigation of some interested persons. 

 4. It is further stated that the petitioners have not received any notice under section 3 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 and, as such, could not make any effective representation to the respondents against their decision for acquisition of the petitioners land. Subsequently, a notice signed by the respondent No. 3 was served upon the petitioners under section 3 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 against which the petitioners sent a Notice demanding Justice through their learned Advocates requesting the respondents to withdraw, rescind and cancel the acquisition of the petitioners' land and, not having received any satisfactory reply to the same, they have been constrained to file these applications under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. 

 5. The respondent No. 3, Additional Land Acquisition Officer, Dhaka as well as added respondent No. 4 Bangladesh Export Processing Zone Authority, hereinafter referred to as BEPZA, are contesting these Rules by filing separate Affidavits-in-Opposition. 

 6. In his affidavit-in-opposition, the respondent No. 3 has stated that for promotion of foreign investment and for resolving the problem of unemployment of this country, the Government, according to Master Plan, took measures for acquiring land measuring 214.34 acres of mouzas Gonokbari and Baipale contiguous to BEPZA under Savar Police Station, Dhaka to extend the area of BEPZA. The proposal was placed before the Government by the BEPZA and was acceded to by the Ministry of Land and thereafter the Government accorded approval dated 26-10-1996 under section 5(1) of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982. On securing approval, notices under sections 3, 4 and 6 of the aforesaid Act, 1982 were served strictly in compliance with law. It has been further stated in the said affidavit-in-opposition that there was no existence of any Mosque or any place of worship at the time of joint survey and at the time of initiation of the said LA case and service of notice under section 3 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982. It has been categorically denied that no notice under section 3 of the aforesaid Ordinance was served upon the petitioners. It has been stated that service of section 3 notice was effected upon the petitioners and the process-server submitted report thereof following which the Writ petitioners' representative one Kazi Shahed Ahmed made representation in writing stating his objection against the acquisition process. According to the acquisition proceedings, appropriate office order/Note were made by the respondent No. 2 in the original LA case and thereafter the authority after hearing the Writ petitioners representative served notices under section 6 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 which has been impugned in the present Writ petitions. It has been further stated that because of the pending Writ petitions possession of the said land could not be taken over by the respondents and compensation paid to the petitioners. 

 7. It has been further categorically stated that the respondents complied with all the provisions of law for acquisition of the aforesaid land for greater public interest and the grounds taken in the Writ petitions are misconceived and deserve no consideration and the impugned orders call for an interference by this Court. 

 8. The respondent No. 4, the Bangladesh Export Processing Zone Authority, in their affidavit-in-opposition have reiterated the facts stated by the respondent No. 3, in that BEPZA in order to extend its area in Dhaka embarked on a plan for acquiring further land under LA Case No. 5 of 1996-1997. It has been further stated that at the time of joint survey no existence of any Mosque or place of worship was found on the petitioners land. It has been further stated that the real owners were offered compensation money and that, in fact, the added respondent No. 4 has already paid the entire compensation money to the respondent No. 2 who would pay the compensation money to the petitioners. It has been further stated that notices under sections 3 and 6 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 were served upon the petitioners and that the petitioners' representatives appeared in the office of the respondents for hearing and making representation against the acquisition process in the LA Case No. 5 of 1996-1997. The grounds taken in the Writ petitions are alleged to be misconceived and the impugned orders call for no interference by this Court. 

 9. Mr Khandaker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing with Mr Mahbubey Alam, learned Advocate, for the petitioners, submits that no notice under section 3 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 having been issued and served upon the petitioners, the entire proceedings of LA Case No. 5 of 1996-1997 has been vitiated and that the impugned orders in the form of notice purported under section 6(1) of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 is no notice in the eye of law and, as such, the acquisition proceedings in respect of the petitioners' land is illegal and without lawful authority. Mr Ahmed next submits that there is a mosque, graveyard and a place used as meditation centre which is visited by eminent people and, as such, it is a place for regular public worship and the acquisition proceedings of the said land is illegal and without lawful authority. In this respect, he has also filed a Supplementary Affidavit with copies of photographs showing part of the building and claims to be a mosque as well as other structures and open space and greenery alleged to be used as place of meditation. The learned Advocate for the petitioners further submits that the selection of the petitioners' land as opposed the land situated to the adjacent of the EPZ area is malafide and not justified and has been designed simply to avoid acquiring the land of most influential persons. The learned Advocate further submits that Gazette Notification has been published in relation to the land acquired in the pending LA case, therefore, the LA case has come to an end/conclusion without acquiring the petitioners' land and that the said land cannot be acquired any more without initiating a fresh LA case. The learned Advocate further submits that though Writ Petitions were filed by several persons including the petitioners challenging the acquisition of 8.50 acres of land, no steps were taken by the respondents for hearing the instant Writ petitions for the last 8 years and the LA case was allowed to proceed in respect of remaining land and thereby the acquisition proceedings having reached a finality in respect of 205.51 acres of land and Gazette Notification having been published in respect of the said land excluding the petitioners' 8.50 acres of land and the respondent No. 4 having demarcated their said 205.51 acres of land by constructing boundary wall, the respondents cannot now proceed to acquire further land in the aforesaid LA case which has already reached its finality by the publication of Gazette Notification. 

 11. As against this, Mr AF Hasan Ariff, the learned Advocate appearing with Mr Md Badruddoza, learned Advocate for the respondent No. 4, BEPZA, submits that the acquisition proceedings of LA case No. 5 of 1996-1997 was done as per provisions of law and that section 3 notice was duly served upon the petitioners. In this respect he drew our attention to Annexure-2 in the affidavit-in-opposition of the respondent No. 3 as well as the reports given by the process server verifying service of notices. He has also drawn our attention to the Annexure-4, a representation given by one Kazi Shahed Ahmed, Editor of the 'Azker Kagoz' dated 5-9-1996 addressed to the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka filing objection to the said acquisition process for the land belonging to him, the description of which appears to be the petitioners' land as well as the copies of the order sheet of the said LA case, particularly order Nos. 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 and 18, Armexure-5 in the respondent No. 3's affidavit-in-opposition indicating that not only section 3 notice was served upon the petitioners but also their representatives were heard. The learned Advocate further submits that there is no existence of any mosque or place of worship or graveyard in the aforesaid land and that the claim of the petitioners is unfounded. Mr Hasan Ariff next submits that the proceedings of LA Case No. 5 of 1996-1997 could not be completed in respect of the petitioners' land due to the pungency of the Writ petitions and an order of stay passed by this Hon'ble Court at the time of issuance of the Rule. LA proceedings in respect of remaining 205.51 acres of land, therefore, proceeded as usual and Gazette Notification was made in due course after obtaining possession of the said land. He, therefore, submits that the question of the petitioners' land being left out of acquisition proceedings for non-publication of the Gazette Notification due to the order of stay of this Court is not tenable in law and is without any substance. 

 12. Mr Fariduddin Khan, the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 3, adopts the arguments of Mr AF Hasan Ariff and submits that notice under section 3 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 was duly served upon the petitioners as evidenced from Annexure-3 series of his affidavit-in-opposition and the subsequent representation by Kazi Shahed Ahmed on behalf of the petitioners, Annexure-4 and other noting’s made in the order sheet of LA case No. 5 of 1996-1997, particularly those order Nos. 13-18 Annexure-5. The learned Assistant Attorney-General further submits that the acquisition process was conducted as per provisions of law and the petitioners not having been able to show any illegality in the acquisition process, the instant Rules are liable to be discharged. 

 14. Section 3 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 requires the service of notice in the prescribed manner at a convenient place or near the property proposed to be acquired. There is no requirement for service of notice personally on the petitioners claiming ownership of the land sought to be acquired. It is sufficient if it is served even near the proceedings land. Annexure-3 series in the affidavit-in-opposition of the respondent No. 3 Additional Land Acquisition Officer are copies of notices believed to be served upon the petitioners. 

 15. On perusal, it appears that appropriate notes were made by the process server at the time of service and subsequently, an objection was filed by Mr Kazi Shahed Ahmed, Editor of the 'Azker Kagoz' by letter dated 5th September, 1996 addressed to the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka mentioning certain objections to the acquisition proceedings. The note sheets in the order sheet of the LA case from 31-8-1996 to 24-9-1996, order Nos. 9 to 18 also clearly reflect receipt of section 3 notice, objection by Kazi Shahed Ahmed on behalf of the petitioners and participation in the hearing. Kazi Shahed Ahmed is the husband of the petitioner in Writ Petition No. 1355 of 1996 and a close relative of all the petitioners whose land is the subject matter of the instant LA case. In this respect, it has been categorically stated that Kazi Shahed Ahmed had other lands which was the subject matter of the instant acquisition proceedings and, therefore, the only conclusion that can be drawn is that he made his objection on behalf of all the petitioners. In such a situation, it cannot be accepted that the petitioners never received any notice under section 3 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982. The petitioners' statements in the Writ petitions that no notice under section 3 was served appears to be false statements, the only purpose of which appears to be to obtain the aforesaid Rules and delay the acquisition proceedings. Needless to say that such practice is seriously deprecated by this Court. 

 16. Next, we refer to Mr Khandaker's submission that Gazette Notification has been published in respect of 205 acres of land of LA Case No. 5 of 1996-1997 and such publication finally ended the LA Proceedings and that the petitioners' 8.5 acres of land not having been included in the said Gazette Notification, is deemed to have been excluded from the instant LA proceedings. LA proceedings started with the service of notice under section 3 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 and ended following Gazette Notification under section 11 of the said Ordinance. In the instant case, acquisition proceedings with respect to the petitioners' land measuring 8.5 acres of land could not be proceeded due to issuance of the aforesaid Rules and orders of stay passed by this Court. Proceedings of LA case, however, continued in respect of remaining land and after award of compensation under section 7, Gazette Notification under section 11 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 was duly completed. The aforesaid land of the petitioners could not be included in the Gazette Notification for the stay orders of this Court issued at their instance and, as such, it does not lie in their mouth to say that the requiring body or acquiring authority deliberately kept the said land outside the Gazette Notification. It is not the petitioners' case that the Government under section 12 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 decided to exclude their lands from acquisition. The object of Gazette Notification under section 11 of the aforesaid Ordinance is to notify the public that such lands have been acquired and vested in the Government. Thus, the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners, in this respect is totally misconceived and has got no merit. 

 18. Mr Khandaker finally submits that there is a mosque and a graveyard and a considerable part thereof is used as a centre for meditation and, as such, as per provisions of section 3 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982, it should be excluded from acquisition proceedings. Though section 3 of the Ordinance makes it mandatory to exclude places of worship we are not satisfied that a place for meditation comes within the definition of place of worship as per provisions of section 151A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. A place for public prayer or religious worship means a public place specifically earmarked, permanently preserved and regularly used exclusively for the purpose of offering prayers or worship by the followers of any particular religion or faith, such as Mosque, Jamatkhana, Eidgah, Temple, Church, Synagogue, Pagoda, etc and includes such adjuncts thereto as are necessary for such purpose and treated as appertaining to such place, but does not include any place used for deriving pecuniary benefit there from. In our opinion, this expression appertaining to the aforesaid provision does not include places for meditation and, as such, the aforesaid land used for meditation cannot be excluded from acquisition proceedings. 

 19. The respondents are strongly denying that there is a mosque and graveyard on the petitioners' land. Whether there is any mosque or graveyard in the proceeding land is a disputed question of fact and we in writ jurisdiction cannot decide such a question. However, for strict compliance of the provisions of law that mosques and graveyards are to be excluded from the acquisition proceedings we hold that if there is any mosque or graveyard on the petitioners' land, the same should he kept outside the acquisition proceedings in accordance with the law.
